item.title: China's nuclear power sector moves toward smarter, greener development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
FUZHOU, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- At the command center of the Ningde nuclear power plant in east China, parameters streamed across a giant screen. A technician put on a smart AR helmet and completed a maintenance inspection in minutes, offering a glimpse of how digital tools are reshaping China's nuclear power industry. The helmet integrates voice interaction, temperature and vibration measurement, and high-intensity lighting. Using diffractive waveguide technology, it projects equipment drawings, work orders and operating procedures into the wearer's field of view. Voice commands are enough to confirm records, said Xiong Shaoyong, a technical specialist at the nuclear base. The system has raised data-entry efficiency by more than 50 percent and improved on-site work efficiency by over 25 percent, Xiong said. The base, the first nuclear power facility in Fujian, now has four units in commercial service. Its second phase, comprising two Hualong One units, is under construction. As digital tools reshape frontline maintenance, China's nuclear power industry is advancing a smarter, more efficient operating model, with digitalization and decarbonization serving as twin engines of high-quality development. At the Ningde base, digitalization is reshaping operations and construction. To address the challenges of densely packed equipment, confined spaces and the risks involved in manual inspections, the plant's operator has built a multi-layered unmanned inspection system and a digital twin platform integrating panoramic imaging, 3D modeling and multi-source data. On the construction site of the next two units, a smart management platform enables real-time monitoring of personnel positioning, tower crane operations and potential safety hazards. "Hualong One is a third-generation nuclear power technology with China's proprietary intellectual property," said a project official responsible for the Phase II project. "Its safety and performance indicators have reached the advanced level of international third-generation nuclear technology, and it has become a signature technology for China's nuclear power industry." Beyond intelligent operations, the base is pursuing green development. A nearly 200-mu (about 13.3-hectare) native white tea plantation grows along the hillsides within the base area, forming what the operator describes as an outstanding ecological demonstration site among nuclear power stations worldwide. Surrounding seawater quality and vegetation coverage have remained stable, while nearby villages have benefited from industrial tourism and other local development opportunities. According to Fujian Ningde Nuclear Power Co., the base's operator, the base had delivered a cumulative on-grid electricity volume of more than 340.24 billion kilowatt-hours by the end of 2025, saving significant amounts of standard coal and cutting carbon dioxide emissions. China had 59 commercial nuclear units in operation by the end of 2025, with a total installed capacity of 62.52 million kW, according to a newly released blue book by the China Nuclear Energy Association. In 2025, nuclear power generated 467.7 billion kWh, accounting for 4.82 percent of the country's total electricity generation and reducing carbon dioxide emissions by roughly 350 million tonnes. A stable and capable domestic supply chain remains central to the sector's development. China has achieved full localization of main nuclear power equipment and independent control of key components, with domestic manufacturers delivering 148 sets of main nuclear equipment in 2025. The industry has formed a complete life-cycle capability covering planning, construction, cold testing and commercial operation, and according to the nuclear energy blue book, it now has the capacity to build up to 50 nuclear units simultaneously. Technological upgrading is accelerating. China General Nuclear Power Corporation has introduced a new generation of intelligent industrial control systems, which provide fault warning, smart monitoring and decision support. Across the country, quadruped robots and autonomous drone systems are being deployed at nuclear power bases to inspect equipment in real time, while Hualong One reactors have entered serial construction. Wang Shoujun, president of the Chinese Nuclear Society, said that promoting the digital and intelligent transformation of China's nuclear industry is an inevitable trend for high-quality development. "AI will serve as a core driver for better quality, higher efficiency and enhanced safety throughout nuclear energy's lifecycle, and nuclear power can underpin the AI sector with stable zero-carbon power," Wang said. ■

item.title: Local industries give China's counties global reach
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
NANNING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Sun Kai made a surprising discovery in Central Asian supermarkets: small mandarins from China were a hit with local shoppers, who affectionately called them "baby mandarins." During visits to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, Sun, 39, a sales manager at Guilin Jolly Cool Fruit Agricultural Products Co., Ltd., saw the fruit selling for as much as 60 yuan (about 8.93 U.S. dollars) per kilogram. "Their love for mandarins, especially the smaller varieties, exceeded our expectations," he said. For Xing'an County, Sun's hometown in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, overseas demand is delivering new opportunities to the citrus industry, a pillar of the local rural economy. The county has more than 200,000 mu (around 13,333 hectares) of citrus orchards, producing over 500,000 tonnes of fruit annually, according to local reports. Sun began exploring overseas markets in 2023 after years in domestic e-commerce and fruit processing. Nanfeng mandarins, a widely grown variety in Xing'an, have proved popular in Central Asia. Newer varieties have pushed down their prices at home, but their small size, sweetness and juiciness appeal to overseas consumers. With support from local authorities, Sun's company worked with village committees to register orchards collectively, helping smaller growers enter overseas markets. The company's export value rose from roughly 500,000 U.S. dollars in 2023 to several million U.S. dollars in 2025, Sun said. Sun estimated that some farming households could earn a combined 50,000 to 60,000 yuan annually from citrus growing and seasonal work in harvesting, sorting and packaging. More than 40,000 households in Xing'an have benefited from citrus exports, while the county's citrus industry is expected to generate over 1.1 billion yuan in output value this year. In neighboring Quanzhou County, another local agricultural specialty is finding customers abroad. Anhe Town has grown taro for more than 1,000 years, aided by its mild climate and fertile soil. Today, the town has approximately 18,600 mu of taro fields, accounting for more than 60 percent of Quanzhou's total. The industry's annual output value has exceeded 100 million yuan for several consecutive years. You Wei, 47, chairman of a Quanzhou-based agricultural company, exports locally grown taro to Malaysia and the Republic of Korea. His company operates a cold-storage facility with a capacity of about 600 tonnes, thus allowing sales beyond the harvest season. "Demand for taro has grown in recent years, driven by increasing interest in healthy eating and the popularity of taro balls in bubble tea," You said. Xing'an and Quanzhou are among a growing number of Chinese counties building on their local strengths to reach overseas markets, aided by improving transportation and logistics networks. Products ranging from agricultural specialties and makeup brushes to wigs, power equipment, tires and toys are finding buyers abroad. In Luxi County in east China's Jiangxi Province, over 140 electric porcelain companies generated 16 billion yuan in revenue in 2025, with exports exceeding 380 million yuan. Meanwhile, Tianchang, a county-level city in east China's Anhui Province, has become one of China's three largest plush toy production bases, with more than 90 percent of local toy products exported to Europe and the United States. Counties contribute approximately 40 percent of China's GDP, according to a think tank report released in late 2025. The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for developing county economies with distinctive local strengths, while the 2026 "No. 1 central document," the first policy statement issued by China's central authorities each year, emphasizes cultivating county-level industries that benefit rural residents. Qiu Tongwei, a professor at Nanjing Agricultural University in east China, said counties should build on their local strengths and pursue distinctive development paths rather than simply copy one another. Yet reaching global markets brings challenges, particularly for inland agricultural exporters facing long transport routes and the need to keep produce fresh. Sun recalled losing an entire truckload of fruit overseas after problems with temperature control and difficulties in communication with a driver. Fruit from Xing'an is generally shipped by sea through Shenzhen in south China or overland via the Horgos border crossing in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Sun hopes the Pinglu Canal, which opened to navigation in September, could eventually offer another shipping option to Southeast Asian markets. Sun plans to register more orchards and introduce more fruit varieties to overseas buyers. "We hope to take mandarins grown along the Xiangjiang River to consumers around the world," he said. ■

item.title: China-Arab cooperation deepening traditional bonds, exploring new horizons
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
NANJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- On the sidelines of the Fifth China-Arab States Political Parties Dialogue being held in the eastern Chinese city of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, an orca-shaped marine robot is outshining other smart devices, such as quadruped robots, in capturing the attention of participants. With streamlined contours and a metallic sheen, the marine robot "Orca Max" developed by Seahi Robotics can operate across the full ocean depth range from 0 to 10,000 meters. When introducing this robot to visitors, Cao Ying, co-founder of the company, said the cooperation meeting offered the Suzhou-based company a valuable opportunity to explore Arab markets. Free from manual remote control, the marine robot can carry out autonomous operations in complex ocean currents, lightless deep-sea zones and areas with no communication coverage. Freddy Elbaiady, vice president of the Egyptian Social Democratic Party and member of Egypt's House of Representatives, stopped at the booth to secure more detailed information about this product. "Egypt boasts numerous ports with strong demand for maritime shipping and vessel maintenance," he said, while adding that the robot has enormous potential in Egypt for vessel cleaning, the construction, operation and maintenance of marine new energy facilities, port inspection, dredging and deep-sea applications. Cao said that the robot has been deployed at more than 70 major ports worldwide. Driven by the company's self-developed AI model, the robot can provide safe, efficient and sustainable general-purpose ocean robotics solutions for global ocean development. The two-day meeting, which opened on Friday, has gathered over 100 leaders of political parties and organizations as well as business, think tank and media representatives from 22 Arab countries. The 2026 dialogue has achieved two milestones: full representation of all 22 Arab countries, and the inaugural China-Arab Business Dialogue on the Belt and Road Initiative as a side event. During the event, entrepreneurs from more than 200 Chinese and Arab firms shared experience on Belt and Road cooperation as well as collaboration in trade, investment, science and technology. Saleh Al Khabti, president of Acwa China, told Xinhua that he was pleased to learn that his hometown, the port city of Jeddah in Saudi Arabia, now has a direct shipping route linking it with Suzhou. The direct container shipping route he referred to opened in October, linking Suzhou's Taicang Port with Jeddah and cutting transit time by two to three weeks. He said the new logistics channel will facilitate trade between China, Saudi Arabia and the broader Middle East. Al Khabti added that the company opened its Beijing office in 2009, and established headquarters in Shanghai in 2023. In 2024, it inaugurated a Global Innovation Center in Pudong District of Shanghai, to foster collaboration in renewable energy, energy storage, green hydrogen and water desalination. "As part of our strategy in China, we aim to invest up to 30 billion U.S. dollars in China by 2030. We also plan to increase our procurement of Chinese equipment by 15 billion dollars annually, and we view Jiangsu Province as a key pillar for tapping promising cooperation opportunities in this area," he said. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the beginning of diplomatic relations between China and Arab countries, as well as the 10th anniversary of the launch of the China-Arab States Political Parties Dialogue mechanism. Figures from the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee show that China has signed Belt and Road cooperation documents with all 22 Arab countries, carrying out more than 200 cooperation projects that benefit nearly 2 billion people on both sides. Bilateral trade between China and Arab countries, meanwhile, reached 422 billion U.S. dollars in 2025. According to the foreign affairs office of the Jiangsu provincial government, green energy and digital intelligence have emerged as new growth drivers for cooperation between Jiangsu and Arab countries. In digital intelligence, autonomous driving technologies developed by firms from Jiangsu are making inroads in the Middle East, where they are helping empower local smart mobility and logistics. In infrastructure, a localised optical fibre and cable production base has been set up in Egypt, while large batches of buses have been exported to Algeria, with a knock-down assembly plant built there. ■

item.title: Chinese premier calls on Chinese, Thai enterprises to lift bilateral cooperation to higher levels
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BANGKOK, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that Chinese and Thai enterprises should follow the prevailing trend and seize opportunities to elevate their cooperation to higher levels. Li made the remarks while attending a symposium with Chinese and Thai entrepreneurs, along with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in Bangkok. After listening to remarks from representatives of both countries' business communities, Li said that as China and Thailand work together to usher in a new golden 50 years of bilateral relations, new opportunities are emerging for economic and trade cooperation. To begin with, China and Thailand enjoy the stability brought by high-level mutual trust and friendship, Li said. In today's world marked by turbulence and uncertainty, stability has become a scarce resource, he said, noting that China-Thailand relations and cooperation have demonstrated strong stability. Close and regular communication between the leaders of the two countries, along with strong people-to-people ties and cultural affinity, has provided businesses in both countries with a stable and predictable environment for expanding investment and making long-term plans, Li said. Growing connectivity between the two countries also brings an aggregation effect, Li said. The steady progress in the construction of the China-Thailand railway, the official opening of China's Pinglu Canal, and the strengthening "soft connectivity" in areas such as trade rules, standards and finance have facilitated more seamless interaction of the two markets, enabling more enterprises to generate greater economic benefits, he added. Flourishing innovative cooperation between the two countries also brings an empowering effect, Li said. China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation continues to expand beyond traditional areas into high-tech, emerging and cutting-edge fields, with new business models and areas of growth constantly emerging, he said. This makes it an opportune time for the two sides to leverage their respective strengths and deepen innovation cooperation, Li said. The two sides should upgrade cooperation from "dining tables and taste buds" to "digital intelligence and green development," Li said, calling for expanding traditional trade in agricultural and food products, advancing agricultural modernization in both countries, and pursuing cooperation in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, clean energy and biomedicine to jointly foster and strengthen new growth drivers. Li called for upgrading cooperation from "production collaboration" to "industrial synergy," adding that the two sides should enhance complementarity and integration in industrial and supply chains, and promote the alignment and mutual recognition of industry standards, to jointly improve competitiveness through more efficient coordination and move up the global value chain. China encourages Chinese enterprises to expand localized operations in Thailand, he added. Li also called for upgrading cooperation from "a bilateral focus" to "regional outreach" by leveraging Thailand's geographic advantages, making good use of policy dividends such as the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and expanding cooperation in third-party markets worldwide to better achieve win-win and multi-win outcomes. The governments of China and Thailand will make active efforts to provide a sound business environment for enterprises of both countries and support their long-term development and deeper engagement in local markets, Li said. He also expressed hope that entrepreneurs from both countries would serve as envoys of friendship among the people and make China-Thailand relations even closer and stronger. For his part, Anutin said China is Thailand's most important trading partner, noting that Thailand hopes to seize the opportunities brought by technological advances and work with China to leverage their respective strengths and achieve higher-quality cooperation. The two countries should move beyond being merely trading partners to becoming long-term partners pursuing common development and mutual success, while further expanding cooperation in electric vehicles, agriculture, investment, connectivity and other areas, Anutin said. Thailand will introduce more policies and measures to create favorable conditions for the long-term operations and development of Chinese enterprises in the country, combat transnational crime and protect the rights and interests of investors, he said. Anutin also expressed confidence that the friendship characterized as "Thailand and China are as close as one family" would yield more tangible results and benefit the peoples of both countries. Speaking at the event, business representatives from both countries briefed the leaders on the progress and outcomes of their cooperation and offered specific suggestions. They expressed full confidence in the China-Thailand friendship and their willingness to further strengthen cooperation and contribute to the development and prosperity of both countries through more practical achievements. ■

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added. ■
